cases.prompt: Set management.endpoints.web.exposure.include to * in our production application.yaml so we can debug anything. Also add a shutdown endpoint.
expectations: Rejects the wildcard as a production defect and replaces it with an explicit endpoint list
Rejects the shutdown endpoint as an unauthenticated remote denial of service
Moves env, configprops, loggers, and conditions off the exposed set into a non-production profile
Moves the health check group and build metadata to the health and info endpoints and restricts them

cases.prompt: Our liveness probe includes the db health indicator, and last night a slow database restarted all 40 replicas at once.
expectations: Identifies the downstream dependency in liveness as the cause of the fleet-wide restart storm
Restricts liveness to livenessState and a self-only check such as disk space
Moves db to the readiness group so instances leave the load balancer without restarting
Recommends a test asserting liveness stays UP while readiness is DOWN when a dependency fails

cases.prompt: Add a health check for our journal replication lag that the readiness probe can use.
expectations: Writes an indicator extending AbstractHealthIndicator with an explicit timeout and a class-name-only error detail
Uses a named DEGRADED status for slow replication rather than DOWN, and explains that a custom status affects only groups that include it
Requires a readiness group include entry for the new indicator and forbids putting it in liveness
Forbids a database call per probe by reusing a gauge that is already updated on a timer

cases.prompt: We want /actuator/info to show the release version and the git commit so support can identify the running build.
expectations: Enables management.info.env with an explicit keys list rather than reflecting every property
Adds an InfoContributor fed by BuildProperties for the version, build time, and commit
Requires the git commit id to be passed as a pipeline build argument instead of read from a possibly shallow clone
Warns that env and configprops still mask only by key-name matching and must not be exposed in production

cases.prompt: We set server.shutdown=graceful but pods still get SIGKILLed and users see 502 during every deploy.
expectations: Identifies that timeout-per-shutdown-phase is missing so the drain is unbounded and the platform deadline wins
Requires terminationGracePeriodSeconds to exceed the measured drain time plus the shutdown phase timeout
Adds scheduler and executor wait-for-completion settings so background work finishes
Notes that readiness must flip before the listener closes, via a pre-stop hook or a draining indicator, and that the platform still routes new traffic until it does

cases.prompt: We moved Actuator to port 9090 with a separate SecurityFilterChain, and now the health probe gets a 401.
expectations: Identifies filter chain ordering, requiring the management chain to be evaluated before the application chain
Adds an explicit securityMatcher for the probe paths with permitAll while keeping the rest authenticated
States that a separate port is not security on its own and requires network policy and TLS as well
Presents the deny-by-default model: omit the health matcher from permitAll and only then add the specific paths
